title: Provisional Admin Token Issuance & Postmortem Controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a safe, auditable, and reversible flow for issuing short-lived provisional admin credentials ("break-glass tokens") that on-call engineers can use during high-severity incidents where normal RBAC elevation paths are unavailable. This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: request surface, approval gates, ephemeral credential creation, mandatory audit metadata, automated expiration/revocation, and a required post-incident review and artifact retention policy.

Scope/Non-goals: Scope includes API endpoints for token issuance (internal only), console UI for emergency requests, control plane audit events, automated revocation jobs, and the postmortem checklist that ties into runbooks and the incident tracker. Non-goals: changing long-term RBAC role definitions, or adding new permanent admin roles.

Design notes:
- Token model: issue JWT-like provisional tokens bound to a single principal, with a max TTL of 15 minutes and single-use flags. Tokens must be cryptographically signed with a dedicated break-glass KMS key so audit logs prove provenance.
- Approval policy: default to quorum-less for P0 incidents using explicit on-call authorization (GitHub on-call roster or PagerDuty webhook). For other severities require either a second human approver or an automated policy check (e.g., service health metrics).
- Audit events: every request/approval/issuance/revocation must emit structured audit entries (actor, rationale, incident id, affected resources, token id, issuance and expiry, approver id, source IP). These events are forwarded to our central audit logging service and retained for 1 year.
- Observable artifacts: token lifecycle dashboard, token issuance heatmap, and a mandatory incident comment in the incident tracker linking to the token id and a brief justification.

Operational guarantees and safeguards:
- Tokens are single-use and bound to a session; replay attempts are rejected with a distinct audit code.
- Automated revocation: a job runs every minute to revoke tokens past TTL or flagged by an approver; revocations emit a revoke audit event.
- Fallbacks: if KMS signing path is unavailable, token issuance is blocked and the system falls back to an offline escalation page that instructs on emergency physical controls (pager escalation).

Acceptance criteria:
1) API + console: create request -> approval -> token = happy path documented and tested in staging.
2) Audit logs: every lifecycle event appears in the audit pipeline with required fields.
3) TTL enforcement: tokens cannot be used after expiry and single-use behavior validated.
4) Post-incident workflow: after use, an automated checklist is generated and assigned to the token issuer and approver for completion before ticket closure.

Security trade-offs: minimizing friction in P0 incidents increases risk surface. Mitigations: short TTLs, single-use binding, mandatory structured justification, immediate revocation capability, and aggressive audit retention and alerting on anomalous issuance patterns.

Docs & links: drafting the runbook and console mockups (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/security/break-glass-design-draft), initial PR for API schema (GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892), and prototype metrics dashboard (Grafana link in internal dashboard).
